questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than those without helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash, no matter what speed you are riding.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than normal.
Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle will not respond as quickly. You should ride slower, slow down sooner, and increase your following distance. You should always warn your passenger about road hazards ahead.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Only use the front brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions one after the other, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: The clothing you wear while riding should protect you from all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips
questions.explanation: Your riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. Good clothing also helps protect you if you crash.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be done on slippery roads to avoid hazards

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires a lot of traction
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of traction to be safe. Avoid making sudden moves like swerving on wet or slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, a group of motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride in the far right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center portion of the lane
Stay in the right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from car doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell riders about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and brakes
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means the rider will turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: When turning, what should you do about braking?

options.text: You can use both brakes safely if you use the right technique.
Braking feels the same as it does on a straight road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can use both brakes safely if you use the right technique.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes to stop quickly while turning, but you must know the proper technique and be very careful.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is not a good idea because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Always wear a riding jacket and long pants when riding in hot weather. Besides keeping you safe from crashes, they also help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what following distance should you maintain?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person age 21 or older is legally intoxicated if their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is at least ______.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person of legal drinking age with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is considered legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while drunk is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What happens if you brake while turning in a curve?

options.text: Braking works the same as on a straight road.
You have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but only with great care. While turning, your tires use some of their grip to lean the motorcycle, leaving less grip available for braking.

questions.question: What does this group riding signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: When group riding, signals help riders communicate with each other. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it means there is a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Slow down, then speed up as you approach it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, then speed up as you approach it.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and slow down as you approach it. Then speed up and ride away. If you encounter a larger animal, brake and prepare to stop.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors and you are not familiar with them, why should you practice?

options.text: Most people do not use mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they also make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Practice using your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex ones.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what is the best thing to do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a wet lane is slippery. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars to avoid the slippery center. The left tire track is usually the best choice.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should wear hearing protection:

options.text: At all times to prevent hearing damage.
Never, because it will block horns and sirens.
Never, if they wear a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing loss, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs protect your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are:

options.text: Usually more powerful than car headlights.
Usually as powerful as car headlights.
Usually less powerful than car headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually less powerful than car headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting it.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in your lane when in traffic. Swerving into another lane to avoid a small animal can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting an animal is safer than hitting a car.

questions.question: When it is raining, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the road is very slippery because oil from cars has not washed away. Riding in the tire tracks left by cars is safest. The left tire track is usually your best choice.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Encourage others to talk them out of driving.
Tell them to take less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to take less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: To prevent drunk driving, arrange other transportation, involve friends to slow their drinking, find excuses to keep them from leaving before they are sober, and get other friends to help stop them.
